New: `intro`, `kinds` (what happens to a document and to an email), `paths` (the S and G paths compared, with the measured golden-set agreement of 2026-09 and the typical cost per document from the call log); the path options say which types can take the S path; only the active processing has a `when` text

intro: Choose a recipe by the files you want to process. Each recipe has its own version number; the number does not rank the recipes.

kinds.document: The system first recognises the document's type (for example an invoice, a utility bill, a bank statement, a certificate; JEV, about 0.0001 USD per document), then extracts the recognised type's fields on the chosen path and checks them in code (for example the tax number's check digit and the totals). If the type cannot be decided, the document gets a to-do.
kinds.email: The system recognises the email's purpose (for example an invoice arrived, a payment confirmation, a question, a newsletter; JEV, about 0.0001 USD per email) and proposes the next step in code. The PDF attachments run as documents, traced back to the email; on request a task proposal is made too.

multi-format-processing.title: Document processing — PDF, Word, Excel, TXT, CSV
multi-format-processing.when: Use this recipe for PDF, DOCX, XLSX, UTF-8 TXT and CSV files. PDF documents follow type-based processing; Word, Excel, text and CSV use GPT to extract facts with source references. JEV can assess those facts. Check reading gaps and the original source before approval.

inputs.label: PDF documents
inputs.description: The system recognises the document type, extracts its fields and checks the results. Uncertain types and values require review.

inputs.label: Word, Excel, TXT and CSV
inputs.description: The reader preserves paragraphs, tables and cell references. GPT proposes facts from the readable content. Images, unsupported structures and missing formula results remain visible gaps; they are not silently treated as read.

path.help: PDF documents and Word, Excel, TXT or CSV files use different extraction paths. Automatic processing supports a mixed package; Word, Excel, TXT and CSV always need GPT extraction.

options.auto: PDF documents use the recognised type's recommended path. Word, Excel, TXT and CSV use GPT extraction followed by JEV support checks. Recommended for mixed document packages.
options.S: For PDF documents only: JEV selects candidate values where the type supports it; other PDF types use GPT and JEV. A package containing Word, Excel, TXT or CSV cannot start on this path. Choose Automatic, GPT + JEV or GPT only for those files.
options.G: GPT extracts values and JEV assesses their support. PDF documents use their type's fields; Word, Excel, TXT and CSV produce facts linked to their source structure.
options.gpt: GPT extracts values without JEV calls. PDF documents also use GPT type recognition. Word, Excel, TXT and CSV retain source references and reading gaps. Source checks do not replace human review.

azure_ocr.help: Azure text recognition applies only to PDF documents. It does not read images embedded in Word or Excel files.

options.on: A weak PDF scan may use Azure recognition within its budget. Word, Excel, TXT and CSV are unaffected.
options.off: Azure recognition is disabled. PDF documents can still use local text recognition; unread images in Word or Excel remain visible gaps.

processing.title: PDF and email processing
processing.when: Use this recipe for PDF documents and downloaded emails. It recognises document types or email intent, processes supported PDF attachments and can propose email tasks. Choose the document recipe for Word, Excel, TXT or CSV files.

inputs.label: PDF documents
inputs.description: The system recognises the document type, extracts its fields and checks the results. Uncertain types and values require review.

inputs.label: Emails
inputs.description: The selected provider recognises email intent. Supported PDF attachments follow document processing; task proposals are optional.

paths.intro: The path says how the system reads the data of a document whose type it has recognised. Either path is followed by the same checks in code, and whatever is uncertain becomes a to-do.
paths.measured: Source of the numbers: the header fields of the golden set (checked sample documents of eight invoice types), and the live (not reused) calls of the call log per document. The S path was measured on 2026-09-30 and the G path on 2026-09-20/21, so the two figures are an indicative comparison only.

rows.label: What it does
rows.S: Code collects the possible values from the text (invoice number, date, amount and name candidates), and JEV chooses among them for each field, or says none of them.
rows.G: GPT reads the data from the text, and JEV checks each field for errors (not truncated, not another field's value, the parties not swapped).

rows.label: Line items
rows.G: Reads them (for example a utility bill's charges and meter readings).

rows.label: Services
rows.S: JEV; on the document types without a JEV path, JEV and OpenAI.

rows.label: Typical cost per document
rows.S: About 0.001–0.002 USD (920 documents in the call log: median 0.0012, mean 0.0023 USD).
rows.G: About 0.007–0.008 USD (588 documents in the call log: median 0.0070, mean 0.0076 USD).

rows.label: Agreement with the golden set (header fields)
rows.G: 940/953 fields (98.6%); better than S on water bills (89/90 against 85/90).

rows.label: Which document types
rows.S: On the eight invoice types (Hungarian and foreign invoices, six utility bills). The other document types have no JEV path; with S chosen they run on the G path (GPT + JEV), so that their data is still read.

rows.label: When it is better
rows.S: For invoice header fields: just as accurate, at a third to a sixth of the G path's cost.
rows.G: When the line items are needed too (utility bills), and on the document types that only have a G path.

path.help: Which tool does the work. The three paths with JEV differ in how the system reads the data of a document of a recognised type; the ‘GPT only’ path works without JEV. Every path is followed by checks in code (for example the tax number's check digit, the totals adding up); whatever is uncertain becomes a to-do.

options.auto: JEV recognises the document's type and the email's intent, and the document type's recommended path runs: S on Hungarian and foreign invoices, G on utility bills (because of the line items), G on the other document types, which only have a G path. Recommended for everyday work.
options.S: Code collects the possible values, and JEV chooses among them for each field. Cheaper; it does not read line items. On the eight invoice types (Hungarian and foreign invoices, six utility bills) only JEV is called. The other document types have no JEV path: they run on the G path (GPT + JEV), so that their data is still read, and so they get an OpenAI budget too.
options.G: GPT reads the data, including the line items, and JEV checks each field for errors. Both JEV and OpenAI calls, so it costs more.
options.gpt: Without JEV, only OpenAI (GPT) works. GPT recognises the document's type (about 0.001–0.002 USD per document), and every document runs on the G path: GPT reads the data and the code checks it (every extracted value must be printed on the document, and the check-digit, amount and required-field checks remain). Measured on the golden set (2026-10-02): GPT recognised the type of 99 of 102 documents (JEV all 102) and stated its 3 errors confidently too; two of them get a to-do (one from a check in code: the type presumes a Hungarian issuer, but GPT says the issuer is not Hungarian), one can pass without a to-do. 27 of the 1010 fields of the 70 golden documents differed from the checked value. GPT also recognises the emails' intent, with the same questions as JEV (94 hits on the 96-email golden set, the 2 errors went to manual review; about 0.0025 USD per email, from a budget of at most 0.07 USD); the PDF attachments run as documents. The run gets no JEV budget, so no JEV call can happen.
options.jev: JEV recognises the email's intent; the PDF attachments run as documents, on the automatic path. This is the default.

arm.help: How the system reads the data of a document whose type it has recognised. Either path is followed by checks in code (for example the tax number's check digit and the totals); whatever is uncertain becomes a to-do.

options.auto: The document type's recommended path: S on Hungarian and foreign invoices, G on utility bills (because of the line items), and G on every other document type, because those only have a G path. Recommended for everyday work.
options.S: Code collects the possible values, and JEV chooses among them for each field. Cheaper; it does not read line items. On the eight invoice types (Hungarian and foreign invoices, six utility bills) only JEV is called. The other document types have no JEV path: they run on the G path (GPT + JEV), so that their data is still read, and so they get an OpenAI budget too.
options.G: GPT reads the data, including the line items, and JEV checks each field for errors. Both JEV and OpenAI calls, so it costs more.

doc_type.help: Internal measurement setting (command line only): every document of the batch runs as this document type, without type recognition.

jev_cache.help: What happens when the same question was put to JEV or GPT before. A question is the same when the model, the instructions and the document's text are all the same; if any of them changes, a new, live call goes out.

options.reuse: The earlier answer can be reused free and at once, for JEV and GPT alike; the same question gets the same answer, so a rerun is free and gives the same result. Recommended for everyday work.
options.live: Every question is a live, paid call; earlier answers are ignored. Needed for measurements (for example to check whether a repeated question gets the same answer); the cost can grow up to the per-item budget.

tasks.help: Whether the system proposes tasks from the emails: what to do, who is responsible, the deadline. Affects emails only.

options.off: No task proposals. The email intent is still recognised and the attachments are still processed. This is the default.
options.propose: GPT makes a proposal for each email. The code checks that every quote in the proposal appears word for word in the email; only a person can accept it. It does not run on emails to be archived. Adds an OpenAI cost per email.

email_text.help: Whether a quote request written in the email itself is extracted from the email's text: the customer, the contact, the deadline and the requested items. Only on emails whose intent is a quote request.

options.extract: The email's own text (its sender, date and subject, without the quoted earlier messages) is extracted like a document: GPT reads it, JEV checks it, and what is uncertain becomes a to-do of the email. About 0.006 USD per such email; every email reserves at most 0.03 USD OpenAI for it, spent only on quote requests. This is the default.
options.off: The email's own text is not extracted. A request form or list attached to the email is still processed as a document.

azure_ocr.help: Whether the system may use the more accurate, paid Azure recognition instead of the local text recognition for a poorly scanned document.

options.on: If the local recognition is weak, the system uses Azure recognition, from a budget of at most 0.02 USD per document. Every call goes into the call log; if the run's Azure budget runs out, the local text is used and the document gets a to-do. This is the default.
options.off: Local recognition only, even for a weak scan. No Azure cost; a weakly recognised document gets the usual recognition to-dos.

unknown_documents.help: A PDF document whose recognised type has no fitting type pack (for example a declaration or a payment reminder) can still yield source-bound facts. The recognised type and its uncertainty stay visible.

options.facts: PDFs without a fitting type pack get general facts from GPT with JEV support, within the run's budget (about 0.08 USD OpenAI and 0.03 USD JEV per document at most). A scan is read with local text recognition and always keeps a to-do saying that its reading is partial. This is the default.
options.review: Such PDFs stop with a manual to-do, as before. No extra provider call.

jev.help: Whether the system uses JEV. Switched off, only OpenAI (GPT) works, together with Azure recognition if that is switched on.

options.on: JEV recognises the document's type and the email's intent, and on the chosen path either chooses among the values (S) or checks what GPT read (G). This is the default.
options.off: Without JEV, only OpenAI (GPT) works. GPT recognises the document's type (about 0.001–0.002 USD per document), and every document runs on the G path: GPT reads the data and the code checks it (every extracted value must be printed on the document, and the check-digit, amount and required-field checks remain). Measured on the golden set (2026-10-02): GPT recognised the type of 99 of 102 documents (JEV all 102) and stated its 3 errors confidently too; two of them get a to-do (one from a check in code: the type presumes a Hungarian issuer, but GPT says the issuer is not Hungarian), one can pass without a to-do. 27 of the 1010 fields of the 70 golden documents differed from the checked value. GPT also recognises the emails' intent, with the same questions as JEV (94 hits on the 96-email golden set, the 2 errors went to manual review; about 0.0025 USD per email, from a budget of at most 0.07 USD); the PDF attachments run as documents. The run gets no JEV budget, so no JEV call can happen.
